operating margin, taxes, capital spending, and working capital to FCFF. FCFF is the cash
available to all capital providers after operating investment, which is why it's discounted using whack
to estimate enterprise value before moving equity value per share. The operating forecast assumes
gradual revenue growth and margin improvements. I treat those as ANOS assumptions rather than
company facts. The model also carries capital spending and working capital investment throughout
the forecast. Because revenue growth alone does not create value, it is required if it requires too
much reinvestment. The bridge then adds cash and selected non-operating assets and subtracts debt
and non-controlling interest to move from enterprise value to the common equity value
used on the per share result. This is the value reset failure scenario. It combines weaker
revenue growth, lower gross margin, higher SG&A, and longer receivable and inventory days.
Those pressures reduce operating profit and FCFF then create funding needs as the cash
balance falls. The point is to test out connected operating problem travels through the income

Pepsi skill will default. The sensitivity grid changes whack and terminal growth. Two assumptions
that matter a great deal because terminal value is 80.1% of enterprise value in the base case.
A high terminal value means long-run assumptions to a substantial weight. The reverse DCF gives a
different view of the market price. Holding the other inputs fixed, reaching the recorded
price requires about 0.85 percentage points more EBIT margin across the forecasting years.
That is one conditional path. Now the markets uniquely identify forecast.
I also included peer lenses for Coca-Cola and Monzels. They are useful reference points
but remain qualified because the peer inputs have comparability limits, including accounting

Combining them without a consistent policy will create false precision.
My committee asks is to defer entry and monitor revenue growth, operating margin,
